samples.identity: Native service trojan with HXB EBankingAssistant version resources and Elastic Farfli signature
evidence: PE headers retain MPRESS section names but executable code is recovered; absolute addresses use original 0x400000 base, unlike header image base 0x45e0000.
0x40663b: GetModuleFileNameA, CopyFileA, CreateServiceA with automatic start type 2, service Description registry write.
0x40607b: reconstructs taskkill /f /im rundll32.exe using stack-byte stores and invokes WinExec with hidden-window argument 0.
Socket send/receive routines at 0x401808 and 0x402072; configuration/string-manipulation routines supply installation paths.

samples.identity: Synthetic multifunction .NET stealer with ransomware and UAC-bypass routines
evidence: Main schedules input capture, screenshot, theft, persistence and impact routines.
HookCallback RVA 0x3720 records timestamp, active window and virtual key; FlushKeylog RVA 0x37f0 sends KEYLOG records through SendToC2.
SendToC2 RVA 0x5ff8 uploads its argument with WebClient.UploadString to configured HTTP URL.
RealEncryption MoveNext RVA 0x4458 enumerates Desktop/TestFolder, reads files, calls EncryptAES, writes .encrypted files and deletes originals.
Encryption is defective: .cctor supplies a 15-byte AES key and 14-byte IV, so set_Key/set_IV fail; ransom text is not evidence of successful encryption.
Multiple unrelated malware mutex names are planted; HiddenTearsMutex/HiddenTearsKey123 do not prove recognized family identity.
